name: Do I need to replace my interior doors when upgrading wall sound insulation?
description: Yes, standard hollow-core doors leak sound easily. Upgrading to a solid-core door with perimeter seals protects your investment in soundproof walls.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace my interior doors when upgrading wall sound insulation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard hollow-core interior doors have virtually no acoustic stopping power and undermine any sound-control work on the adjacent wall. A typical hollow door has a low sound transmission class, and sound freely passes through the gap beneath it. Replacing it with a solid-core wood or composite door adds significant mass. Additionally, installing perimeter acoustic jamb gaskets and an automatic drop-seal at the threshold creates an airtight perimeter when closed. A decision factor when planning a wall upgrade is recognizing that if you invest in double-stud or decoupled walls, retaining a standard hollow door will leave a direct leak that negates your investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, standard hollow-core doors leak sound easily. Upgrading to a solid-core door with perimeter seals protects your investment in soundproof walls.
